article_title: Designing Academic Writing Analytics for Civil Law Student Self-Assessment
citation: Knight, S., Buckingham Shum, S., Ryan, P., Sándor, Á., & Wang, X. (2016). Designing Academic Writing Analytics for Civil Law Student Self-Assessment. Int J Artif Intell Educ. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-016-0121-0
title: Rhetorical move typology of salient sentences for analytical writing analytics
description: The XIP rhetorical parser detects sentences conveying rhetorical moves in analytical texts, building on Swales' concept of rhetorical moves as communicative functions in scholarly argumentation. AWA labels salient sentence types: Summarizing issues (S), Background knowledge (B), Contrasting ideas (C), Emphasizing important ideas (E), Novel ideas (N), Surprising facts (S), open Questions (Q), and research Trends (T). Detection relies on "syntactically related words and expressions that convey constituent concepts", e.g. a pair conveying 'contrast' plus 'idea/mental operation' signals a Contrasting idea sentence.
requirements: Dedicated lexicons listing words and expressions associated with constituent concepts
Pattern-matching rules selecting sentences with syntactic dependencies instantiating concept pairs
constraints: The typology is designed to be modified if a new domain establishes the need for additional rhetorical moves
The parser does not yet analyse or provide feedback above the sentence-level
target_learners: higher education students writing analytical essays
target_learning_goals: recognising rhetorical structure in academic argumentation
examples: Sentences containing 'challenge...identify', 'highlights...need', and 'demonstrating...failure' are all labelled 'C' because bold words match the contrast + idea/mental operation pattern
